rules.statement: Python computes every median, position and outlier. A peer you assess Comparable or Partly comparable is included in them, and a Not comparable peer is shown but kept out of every statistic, so choose each `comparability` with that effect in mind; `rules` of the module context gives the minimum number of included peers.
rules.from_code: {"inclusion": "Comparable and Partly comparable peers are included; a Not comparable peer is shown but kept out of every statistic", "minimum_included_peers": 3, "outlier_fraction": "0.5", "position": "1 + the number of entities strictly better than the issuer among the included peers with a value and the issuer; ties share a position"}

rules.statement: Write exactly one assessment for each peer listed in `peers.rows` of the module context, its `peer` the row's `label` written exactly, and none for another name or twice. When the peers source is absent, write no assessment.

Every assessment lists `evidence`, and a Partly comparable assessment states its `limitation`. `overall.confidence` is never High, because the peer figures are desk-supplied and unaudited. A peer whose `period_end` is more than 12 months before the end of CP-1's LTM period is never Comparable: assess it Partly comparable with its `limitation`, or Not comparable.

Each `rationale` is nonblank run text with no bare figure (digits only inside a period or filing label); a figure appears only as `{ref|unit}` with a `ref` and `unit` listed in `cp1_facts`, closed and non-empty; a reference that resolves to no fact, or to a fact whose value is a gap, is refused. State no instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion in any text field (`rationale`, `limitation` and gap fields), and leave none blank: a blank `limitation` (of an assessment, when given, or of `overall`) or gap field (`gap`, `why_it_matters`, `affected_analysis`, `action`) is refused. A fiscal-year label (`FY2025`, `fiscal 2025`) written up to the next `.`, `;` or `:` beside a `{ref|unit}` must be a year of the period of a figure referenced there.
Cite each quote verbatim under the locator of its page, and read that page with `read_pages` first; call only the offered tools.
